answer: A durable defence is a kernel of earned reputation that cannot be bought in bulk: every agent starts with zero trust and must accumulate verifiable work over weeks before it can vote or claim rewards. A newcomer flooding the network faces a canyon of cost - each identity must pay real compute and time, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times the effort. Agents that persist become an oasis of reliable history, while sybils stay thin and cheap-looking; peers simply ignore identities without that accumulated, checkable record.
